feature1.prompt: The duration-only expressions currently fail on SQLite and MySQL due to issues in the underlying database operations. In this feature, the focus is on simplifying the backend by removing the problematic date_interval_sql method. This method, previously used in several database backend operations, is considered redundant and contributes to the observed conversion errors when handling duration fields. After the fix, adding a timedelta to a DurationField should not trigger a conversion error, and the database operations should no longer reference the removed method.
feature1.hint_texts: Begin by eliminating the date_interval_sql method from the base operations as well as its implementations within the MySQL and SQLite backends. Specifically, remove the method definitions from the files django/db/backends/base/operations.py, django/db/backends/mysql/operations.py, and django/db/backends/sqlite3/operations.py. Ensure that any calls to date_interval_sql are also removed or refactored so that the backend uses the newer mechanisms for duration arithmetic. This cleanup will reduce redundancy and prevent the conversion errors observed in the problem statement.
feature1.entrypoint: Files to modify: django/db/backends/base/operations.py (remove the date_interval_sql method definition), django/db/backends/mysql/operations.py (delete the implementation of date_interval_sql), and django/db/backends/sqlite3/operations.py (delete the implementation of date_interval_sql). Focus on the code blocks where the method is defined and called, as indicated in the diff patch.

tests.FAIL_TO_PASS: test_date_interval_sql (tests/backends/base/test_operations.py) [this test is removed to reflect the removal of the date_interval_sql method]
tests.PASS_TO_PASS: All other backend operation tests that do not rely on date_interval_sql should continue to pass.

feature2.prompt: The duration-only expressions are failing on SQLite and MySQL when combining a DurationField with a timedelta value, resulting in conversion errors. This feature focuses on refactoring the ORM expression handling to correctly process duration arithmetic. The aim is to improve the handling within the Combinable and DurationExpression classes so that adding a timedelta to a DurationField yields the correct result. After the fix, operations such as annotating a model instance with a duration expression should work seamlessly without any conversion errors.
feature2.hint_texts: Update the ORM by modifying the logic in django/db/models/expressions.py, specifically within the Combinable and DurationExpression classes. Revise the _combine and as_sql methods to better handle instances when a timedelta is added to a DurationField, checking for the field’s internal type rather than relying on outdated constructs. Ensure that the expression compilation paths correctly distinguish duration arithmetic from other types of arithmetic. Use the diff patch as guidance for adjusting the conditionals and refactoring the DurationExpression.compile and as_sql methods.
feature2.entrypoint: File to modify: django/db/models/expressions.py. Review and update the implementation of Combinable._combine, Combinable.as_sql, and both the compile and as_sql methods in DurationExpression. Focus on the sections where duration fields are processed and where datetime.timedelta values are converted. The diff patch provided offers a clear starting point by showing how conditional checks and output field handling were adjusted.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the ORM’s handling of duration fields and arithmetic, sharing common code in the database operations and expression compilation modules. The DurationField and related methods in django/db/backends and django/db/models/expressions serve as shared components.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1’s removal of the date_interval_sql method should be coordinated with Feature2’s refactoring to ensure that no backend functionality is broken by the removal. It is imperative that any fallback logic in the expression compilation correctly functions without the removed method. The integration will involve verifying that the ORM correctly handles duration arithmetic end-to-end on different database backends.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature1 and Feature2 must discuss the new API for duration handling and agree on the proper method of converting timedelta values. Regular coordination is needed to confirm that changes in backend operations do not inadvertently affect expression handling. Both teams should plan integration tests and share their implementations early to address any dependencies.
